messages.subject: Re: timeDate package for renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tomas,
Sorry for the late response,

Renjin's S4 implementation still has some issues, notably during package loading, which are probably affecting this package.

The output you see on packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org> is from building the original source package from CRAN:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/timeDate/index.html

You can grab the sources from CRAN and step through the namespace evaluation step to see where things are going wrong.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: semicolon issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a problem with using a semicolon in one line. For testing I use renjin command line tool:

fujdiar@pc:~$ renjin
Java home = /usr/lib/jvm/java-7-oracle
Using local repository: /home/fujdiar/.m2/repository
> A=1; B=3
> A
[1] 1
> B
ERROR: object 'B' not found
>

when I run similar code from java I got same issue

but when I try this:
> {A=1; B=3}
> B
[1] 3
> A
[1] 1
>
everything seems to be OK

for example in Rstudio  braces are not necessary
> A=1;B=3
> A
[1] 1
> B
[1] 3
>

is this bug(known/unknown) or "standard" behavior

thanks in advance

messages.subject: Re: semicolon issue
messages.body_plain:
Stanislav,

this is a known issue, see https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/79, but I have added a comment that the code does work when you use the braces.
​
Regards,

Maarten-Jan

messages.subject: issue with transform list to matrix or unboxing raw vectors
messages.subject_clean: issue with transform list to matrix or unboxing raw vectors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Our quants use a lot of heterogeneous lists:

A = list(a, c(2,3), 4, c(5,6))
then transformation to matrix
M = matrix(A, 2, 2, byrow=TRUE)

after that operation we have a problem with unboxing
if I do this
> M[1,1]
[[1]]
[1] 1
everything is ok but if I want to go in to structure
> M[[1,1]]
NULL

but if I use some helper variable
> H = M[1,1]
> H[[1]]
[1] 1
>

so I don't have direct access to fields of matrix, but I can access to fields of original list:
> A[[1]]
[1] 1
and strength is that I can do something like
M[[1]] like in list in spite of it is matrix
> M[[1]]
[1] 1

Can you help me with that is something what I do wrong(or I've read documentation inattentively)?
